reflection.text:
Reflection after unblinding to epothilone B (PubChem CID 448013, ChEMBL Tubulin stabiliser) - verdict correct with call Microtubule stabilizers p=0.94.

What the evidence got right and why:
- Acquisition strategy was efficient. Starting with list_available_experiments (e1: 8 doses 0.001-3 uM, 4 wells budget) I sampled mid-high dose first (e2: w_2e25395163 0.3 uM tub_glcm_contrast z=+154.7, tub_std +77.4, tub_mean +42.1) and highest dose (e3: w_56c0ae0535 3 uM +121.7, +69.7, nuc_solidity -39.8) to establish dynamic range without saturating toxicity. This immediately captured the massive, positive-direction tubulin signal opposite to the loss expected for Microtubule destabilizers or Actin disruptors.
- Comparison to reference atlas discriminated correctly. e4 at 2 wells: NSC 2/2 stabilizers, k-neighbours 6/10 stabilizers vs 4/10 destabilizers; e8 at 4 wells: NSC 3/4 stabilizers, 6/10 vs 2/10 destabilizers + 1/10 Actin disruptors, similarity 0.79-0.86 vs next class ~0.57 noted in review. The consistent top class across two independent atlas queries was key.
- Phenotype description broke the tie. e5: microscopist on 4 fields, density lower vs DMSO, 9 observations, candidates Microtubule stabilizers = thick bundling morphology, not depolymerization/fragmentation. This distinguished the same tubulin texture metrics from a destabilizer artifact.
- Dose mapping confirmed monotonicity and ruled out off-target. Adding e6 low dose (0.01 uM z=+5.5, +5.2) and e7 mid dose (0.1 uM +28.0, +33.1, +18.3) gave dose_response e9 tub_glcm_contrast rho=+0.80 and e10 tub_mean rho=+0.80 dose-ordered to 0.3 uM then plateauing, plus e11 cell_count rho=-0.80 consistent with mitotic arrest/cell loss. Effect reproduced across 4 independent dose wells and 3 orthogonal analyses (atlas, dose-response, microscopy).

What misled or was missed and why:
- No single measurement was misleading in direction, but magnitude alone could be ambiguous: actin metrics also rose secondarily but smaller than tubulin, and early k-neighbours included 40% destabilizers (e4) which reflects shared mitotic arrest features in the shared space. Directionality (gain vs loss) and microscopist bundling were required to resolve this; without e5 I would have over-relied on texture z-scores.
- Statistical power was missed by design. All dose_response p=0.2 due to n=4 wells, single replicate per dose. I acquired no replicate of the same dose, as noted in review budget exhausted 0/4 left. Formal significance was lacking, so inference rested on huge effect sizes (z +5 to +155) and reproducibility across doses rather than p-values.
- I performed no within-run biochemical orthogonal test; next step proposed was live-cell polymerization + phospho-histone H3 washout, which was appropriate but not executed in screen.

Why acquisition choices mattered: sequential broadening from mid-high/high to low/mid established onset at ~0.01-0.1 uM and saturation at 0.3 uM, making the dose trajectory interpretable with only 4 wells. Updating hypotheses at step 12 after e8 was justified; p=0.94 was calibrated given convergent evidence.

Unblinding check: ChEMBL MECHANISM Tubulin stabiliser and name/BBBC021 structure agree for epothilone B, consistent with literature returned in this run that annotates epothilone B as a microtubule stabilizer PMID 12802795, PMID 39147581, PMID 41224993, PMID 25765066. Second literature query on phenotype bundling returned 0 hits, so no additional phenotypic reference was available in this run.

This reflects high-content screening data for research use only, not clinical advice.

If this were a real lab I would proceed with the proposed tubulin polymerization assay vs stabilizer/destabilizer controls around 0.01-0.3 uM with mitotic markers to confirm reversibility of bundles.
